newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly higher on Tuesday with early-maturing contracts rising sharply due to increased demand for funds linked to new domestic A share issues, traders said.
Securities houses were seen borrowing heavily, especially in the seven-day contract, to prepare to bid for newly offered shares, traders said.
Wan Nianqing Cement Co is scheduled to issue 45 million A shares on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Wednesday.
"The new issue fanned short-term fund demand on Tuesday, pushing up the repo rates," one trader said.
Traders said they expected contracts to rise slightly on Wednesday due to the new A share issue.
The sfwen-day contract was the most actively traded on Tuesday, ending up at 8.80 percent from 7.70 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 2.05 million lots from 2.45 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
But the weak performance of the domestic A share markets overall convinced some institutions to stay on the sidelines, and that held turnover down, traders said.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly higher on Tuesday mainly because short-term funds continued to flow into the spot market from the nation's weak stock markets, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in July 2006 rose to 113.83 yuan from 113.41 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose sharply to 1.30 million lots from 759,456 lots with new liquidity flowing in to the market, traders said.
Traders said they expected stock market weakness to benefit these contracts as well.
